label: Digitally Immersed & Emotionally Distressed
summary: This profile represents highly educated women who spend more than 5 hours daily online and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. With a UCLA-8 loneliness mean of 1.74, a PHQ-9 depression mean of 1.75, and a notably high GAD-7 anxiety mean of 2.17, this group consistently scores above moderate thresholds across all three psychological distress dimensions. Their extensive screen time may both reflect and reinforce patterns of social isolation and emotional difficulty.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, daily screen time exceeding 5 hours
behavior_markers: Extended daily screen time (more than 5 hours)
Co-occurrence of loneliness, depression, and anxiety suggesting compounded emotional distress
High educational attainment paired with significant psychological burden

label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report consistently low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. With UCLA-8 loneliness scores well below the scale midpoint, minimal PHQ-9 depression scores, and near-floor GAD-7 anxiety scores, these individuals demonstrate strong psychological well-being across all three measured dimensions.
demographic_anchor: Male, holding a graduate degree or above, with 1–3 hours of daily screen time or social media use
behavior_markers: Reports very low loneliness on the UCLA-8 scale (mean ≈ 0.77)
Exhibits minimal depressive symptoms on the PHQ-9 (mean ≈ 0.33)
Shows near-absent anxiety symptoms on the GAD-7 (mean ≈ 0.09)
Maintains moderate and limited screen time (1–3 hours daily)
Demonstrates consistently positive mental health indicators across all assessed domains

label: Lonely but Emotionally Resilient
summary: This profile captures respondents who report notably elevated loneliness yet maintain relatively low levels of depressive and anxiety symptoms. Despite feeling socially disconnected, they appear to manage their emotional well-being without significant clinical distress, suggesting a pattern where subjective loneliness does not necessarily translate into broader mood or anxiety disorders.
demographic_anchor: Predominantly female, holding graduate-level or higher education, reporting 1–3 hours of daily social-media or screen-related activity
behavior_markers: Elevated loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.30) indicating moderate-to-high perceived social isolation
Low depressive symptom burden (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.86) suggesting subclinical depression levels
Low anxiety symptom burden (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.91) indicating minimal generalized anxiety
Moderate daily screen or social-media use (1–3 hours), neither extremely low nor high
Possible reliance on academic or professional engagement as a coping mechanism, given high educational attainment
Social disconnection that may reflect quality-of-connection concerns rather than absence of social contact
tone: Quietly isolated yet psychologically composed; reflective and self-sufficient rather than overtly distressed
